_schema_note: Every string appears on a slide exactly as written — format numbers as they should display ($3.1M, 94%). cost.chart labels/values MUST be in ascending value order. illustrative:true appends a placeholder disclaimer to every slide's speaker notes.

meeting.title: Vendor consolidation
meeting.subtitle: Proposal to the Q3 board — decision requested by October 1
meeting.notes: Frame: one decision today — approve consolidation so Wave 1 starts in October.

recommendation.title: Recommendation: consolidate 142 vendors to 38, for $3.1M annual savings

stats.label: vendors after consolidation
stats.detail: top 20 renegotiated; tail spend on one platform

recommendation.kicker: Complete by end of Q1 2027. Wave 1 starts October 6 if approved by October 1.
recommendation.notes: Talk track: lead with the number — the ask funds itself in four months. Sources: savings model v3 (procurement), AP trailing-12-month extract.

trend.title: Vendor count grew 2.4x in three years, with no single approval owner

chart.caption: Active vendors with ≥1 paid invoice in trailing 12 months (illustrative)

paragraphs.text: Spend stayed near $31M per year while the vendor count rose from 59 to 142.
Average spend per vendor fell from $525K to $218K. Small contracts carry full onboarding, security review, and invoicing overhead.
Any budget owner can add a vendor. No role is accountable for the total.

trend.notes: Talk track: growth was organic, not a decision anyone made — that is the governance gap. Source: AP vendor master.

cost.title: Fragmentation costs $4.2M per year; consolidation recovers $3.1M
cost.takeaway: 37 tools overlap an existing capability; 14 categories split volume across 3+ suppliers, below every discount tier. The unrecovered $1.1M sits in contracts we keep for capability or risk reasons.
cost.notes: Talk track: three cost pools, largest first; we recover about three quarters of the total. Sources: license inventory audit, AP category analysis.

options.title: Targeted consolidation has the best return for the risk taken
options.footnote: Full consolidation saves $700K more but forces 26 extra migrations and concentrates category risk.
options.notes: Talk track: full consolidation is the tempting number — walk through why the extra $700K is not worth 26 more migrations. Source: options model, procurement + IT joint estimate.

timeline.title: Three waves complete the consolidation by end of Q1 2027

waves.name: Wave 2 · Dec 2026–Jan 2027
waves.action: Renegotiate top-20 contracts at pooled volume

waves.name: Wave 3 · Feb–Mar 2027
waves.action: Move tail spend (58 vendors) to one procurement platform

timeline.kicker: Wave 1 requires the October 1 approval. Waves 2 and 3 proceed only if the December review confirms savings are tracking.
timeline.notes: Talk track: sequencing is risk control — easiest exits first, renegotiation from committed volume, tail last. Source: wave plan, VP Procurement.

risks.title: The top three risks have funded mitigations and named owners
rows: 30-day parallel run for every exited tool; rollback plan per migration
Retained vendors raise prices after exits
3-year rate locks signed before any exit is announced
Legal review of top-20 contracts before Oct 1; fees capped within the $850K budget
risks.notes: Talk track: each mitigation is funded inside the $850K envelope; no contingency ask will follow. Source: risk register, joint Legal/IT/Procurement review.

ask.title: The ask
ask.statement: Approve vendor consolidation by October 1: $850K one-time budget and the top-20 renegotiation mandate.
rows: CFO, with board approval at the Q3 meeting
December board meeting — Waves 2–3 proceed only if savings track to plan
ask.notes: Close: restate the single decision and the date. First board-visible checkpoint is the December review gate.
